subject: physics
question_text: Why does a car with flattened tyres stop sooner than one with inflated tyres?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 5 VERY SHORT ANSWER. The 1+1 mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Why friction is more
lines: A flattened tyre deforms much more and
touches the road over a larger area.
steps.margin_note: Name ROLLING friction. "More friction" alone does not say which kind.
steps.why: Rolling resistance comes from energy lost as the tyre flexes and un-flexes. A soft tyre flexes more on every turn, so it loses more energy per metre.
common_mistakes: Writing sliding friction. The wheel is rolling, not skidding.

recall.must_convey: That a flat tyre deforms more and has a larger contact area, so rolling friction increases.
accept: tyre ekkuva deform ayi rolling friction perugutundi

steps.memory_tip: A flat tyre bends more at every turn, and that bending wastes energy — rolling friction rises.

steps.label: Why it stops sooner
lines: An inflated tyre deforms less, so it
steps.margin_note: Close the loop — more friction, shorter distance. Answer the question that was asked.
steps.why: The car is losing kinetic energy faster, so it runs out of speed over a shorter distance.
common_mistakes: Stopping at "friction is more" without saying what that does to the car.

recall.must_convey: That the larger rolling friction makes the car stop sooner.
accept: more friction so it stops sooner

steps.memory_tip: More rolling friction removes kinetic energy faster, so the car stops in less distance.

insider_note: The examiner is checking for the word ROLLING. "More friction", without naming which kind, does not earn the first mark.
